perspective: Adversarial lifecycle-boundary verification across Mayra intake, Laura/HR processing, Oracle assignment records, and Daisy/Finance monitoring.

findings.claim: An open position is an authorized staffing need or slot, not an appointment, request, employee, or assignment.
evidence: Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:238-267 — discussion distinguishes positions/roles to fill from requests and tracks faculty non-response.
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:311-323 — Mayra's work includes tracking open positions and asking supervisors whether positions should be renewed.
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:496-504 — positions depend on budgets and are not a fixed appointment list.
findings.risk: Treating an open position as a person or appointment would create phantom hires, lose headcount/budget context, and conflate demand with execution.
findings.recommendation: Keep position identity, supervisor, job code/type, budget/headcount context, and open/filled/closed state separate from person/request/appointment records.

findings.claim: A request is an intake or amendment event; it is not proof that a position exists, an appointment is approved, employment is active, or a termination occurred.
evidence: Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:12-20,44-52 — faculty email requests are collected before Mayra enters worksheet data.
HR App (1).docx:792-805,1087-1096 — direct faculty requests occur, but intended student-request intake is through Mayra; Laura acts from the tracked worksheet.
change_requests.json:18-27,95-105 — prior verification separates requester, Mayra intake, and downstream executor; derived D4 routing is too strong.
findings.risk: A request-to-status shortcut could cause unapproved changes, duplicate appointments, or premature termination.
findings.recommendation: Persist request type, requester, submitter, target position/appointment/assignment, requested values, receipt time, and disposition separately from execution state.

findings.claim: An appointment is a time-bounded employment arrangement with terms; it is not identical to a student/person, Oracle assignment row, or current active employment.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:68-78 — appointment terms include job code/name, supervisor, hours, salary, and start/end dates.
HR App (1).docx:561-563 — appointment changes and separate assignments are distinct Oracle operations.
HR App (1).docx:962-987 — spring changes can require a new process while unchanged rows need no Laura action.
findings.risk: A person-level row cannot represent multiple concurrent assignments, separate effective periods, or changed terms without collapsing history.
findings.recommendation: Use separate person, appointment-term, and assignment identities with effective dates and revision links.

findings.claim: An assignment is the Oracle-level work unit; one student can have multiple assignments, and an added assignment creates a second assignment number.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:561-563 — Laura distinguishes changing an assignment from adding a separate assignment record/number.
oracle_hr.json:6-15 — prior verification identifies assignment identity as distinct from student identity.
student_hiring_pipeline.md:43-46,123 — derived artifact records additional assignments and assignment-level unit of work.
findings.risk: Using student identity as the lifecycle key can merge TA/RA or other concurrent work and apply changes or termination to the wrong record.
findings.recommendation: Make assignment ID/Oracle assignment number mandatory for assignment-scoped changes, costing, verification, and termination.

findings.claim: Screening, authority signature, student signature, Oracle entry, HR verification, and Finance costing are workflow gates/events; none alone proves active employment.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:78-89,523-548 — screening, drafted/signed offer, student DocuSign, and Oracle entry are separate steps.
HR App (1).docx:120-130 — entered records can wait in approval, disappear, require checking, and only then become verified; new hires also require pre-boarding.
HR App (1).docx:121-130 and Daisy Matos.docx:1022-1049 — verified is a handoff to Finance work, not a stated employment-active declaration.
findings.risk: Conflating verified, signed, costed, or paid with active employment can expose people who never started, miss pending approvals, or retain ended appointments as active.
findings.recommendation: Maintain independent states for screening, signatures, Oracle submission/approval/verification, pre-boarding, employment-active, and costing. Define the authoritative active predicate before reporting.

findings.claim: Reappointment/renewal is a new term decision using prior data as a proposal; it is not automatic continuation and not the same as adding a new assignment.
evidence: Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:44-52,64-86 — prior-semester data is shown for confirmation/editing; chartfields may change and automatic renewal is rejected.
HR App (1).docx:962-987 — copied spring rows can remain unchanged or require a new change process.
renewals.json:5-50 — prior verification preserves copied snapshot, confirmation, and changed-row semantics.
findings.risk: Auto-renewing or treating a copied row as active approval can carry stale funding, hours, rates, or dates into a new term.
findings.recommendation: Create a distinct reappointment/renewal request and next-term appointment revision linked to the prior term; record confirmation, edit, outstanding, and no-renewal outcomes.

findings.claim: A change is an amendment/revision to an existing appointment or assignment, not an in-place overwrite and not automatically a new person or new position.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:780-851 — completed TA/RA terms may change; Laura needs a new offer letter and Oracle amendment.
HR App (1).docx:1023-1053 — funding changes must be visible to Finance and request history retained for audit.
change_requests.json:5-16,31-52,81-105 — prior verification rejects silent overwrite and generic approval assumptions.
findings.risk: Mutating the current row destroys before/after terms and can desynchronize offer, Oracle, Finance, and audit records.
findings.recommendation: Represent amendment request, proposed revision, effective date, authorization/confirmation, downstream execution, and superseded prior values separately. Leave screening/signature re-run rules owner-defined.

findings.claim: Termination is a requested and executed lifecycle transition with an effective date; removing an item from an active summary is not deletion of the historical appointment.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:1045-1058,1087-1096 — student termination should be submitted through Mayra and retained as a request/history item.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:892-905 — Finance terminates ended records in its worksheet and they disappear from the active summary.
finance_monitoring.json:41-50 and change_requests.json:54-65 — prior verification distinguishes summary removal from durable termination and requires preserved history.
findings.risk: A delete or unrestricted status edit can hide an active assignment, erase effective-date/audit evidence, or fail to update Oracle/payroll/costing.
findings.recommendation: Use termination_requested, confirmed/authorized, effective, executed, and downstream-reconciled states; preserve the appointment/assignment historically and define executor/authority.

findings.claim: Historical record is an append-only or otherwise preserved account of requests, terms, changes, signatures, verification, costing, and termination; it is not the current-state row.
evidence: HR App (1).docx:696-701 — spreadsheet overwrites lose the original request and audit trail.
HR App (1).docx:1045-1058 — audit evidence was difficult to recover; one-place request history is required.
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:188-196 and Daisy Matos.docx:1035-1049 — change history, notes, status, date, and initials are requested/used.
change_requests.json:81-92 — prior verification recommends field-level before/after audit events.
findings.risk: A mutable current-state record cannot prove what was requested, approved, executed, superseded, or terminated at a past time.
findings.recommendation: Keep immutable event/history records linked to current projections; never reconstruct history from the latest appointment row or summary filter.

findings.claim: The unified workflow currently conflates lifecycle axes in its derived summaries, especially request/position ownership, verified/active employment, and termination/history.
evidence: mayra_student_hiring_flow.md:47-80 — marks the mid-semester form-link path confirmed despite the transcript describing it as proposed; assumes Laura-before-Daisy ordering.
student_hiring_pipeline.md:43-46,97-114 — models change as a single loop and uses verified as the terminal handoff to costing without a separate employment-active state.
finance_accounts.json:84-95 — broad-read proposal conflicts with Finance sensitivity boundary; finance source authority and completion state remain unresolved.
finance_monitoring.json:78-85 — active, stale, superseded, extended, ended, and terminated are explicitly unresolved.
findings.risk: A single status field or unified linear state machine will permit invalid transitions and inaccurate active-appointment reports.
findings.recommendation: Replace one-dimensional status with typed linked entities plus independent state dimensions: position, request, appointment term, assignment, HR workflow, employment activity, finance costing, termination, and history.

missing_or_ambiguous: Authoritative definition of open/filled/closed position and headcount or budget authorization.
Canonical appointment identity and whether effective-dated Oracle records are the authority.
Authoritative active-employment predicate, including start-date, pre-boarding, approval, end-date, leave, supersession, and payroll conditions.
Whether reappointment creates a new appointment version, a new assignment, or an effective-dated Oracle change; confirmation/no-response deadlines are unspecified.
Change-specific rules for repeated screening, hiring-authority signature, student signature, Finance re-verification, and assignment/version creation.
Termination authority, confirmer, effective date, Oracle/payroll/costing actions, and idempotent repeat behavior.
Whether historical records must be technically immutable/append-only, retention duration, and permitted corrections.
Exact post-Oracle and post-Finance states; `verified`, `costed`, the Daisy status heard as `page`/possibly `paid`, and `active` are not interchangeable.
Role/field-level visibility and edit permissions, especially sensitive Finance data versus cross-team operational views.
Whether the mid-semester OPS form and any automated integrations are current behavior or future design.
